kinds.d: Instrument that shows air pressure, and so the likely weather, with a mercury column or a sealed aneroid capsule.

x.d: Upright mercury-tube barometer in a narrow case, the original form after Torricelli's 1643 experiment.

v.d: adjustable mercury cistern for exact readings, named after Jean Nicolas Fortin

x.dt: mahogany or oak case · cistern or siphon tube · vernier scale

x.d: Mercury barometer whose float turns a pointer round a dial, in a banjo-shaped case; popular in Britain from about 1810.
x.dt: banjo case · dial with weather words · often with thermometer and hygrometer

x.d: Mercury barometer with thermometers and printed rules for forecasting, after Admiral Robert FitzRoy; made for homes after his death in 1865.

v.d: oak case, dry and wet thermometers

x.d: Gimballed mercury barometer with an iron cistern that became the standard on Royal Navy and other ships in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
x.dt: brass tube · iron cistern · gimbals · attached thermometer

x.d: Mercury barometer built to be read at sea, from Robert Hooke's 1668 design onward.
Barometer using a sealed metal capsule instead of liquid, invented by Lucien Vidi in 1844; the common household form.

v.d: Short & Mason with Taylor Instrument Companies

x.dt: brass or wood case · dial · ship's-wheel and porthole styles

kinds.d: Barometer that records air pressure over time as a line on a paper chart turned by clockwork.

x.d: Stacked aneroid capsules move a pen across a chart on a clockwork drum turning once a day, week or month; heyday late Victorian to early 20th century.
x.dt: glazed wooden case · ink pen · weekly chart

x.d: Recording barometer from the Paris firm of Jules and Max Richard, whose 1880s recorders set the pattern; marked with the RF monogram.

kinds.a: chemical weather glass · FitzRoy's storm barometer
kinds.d: Sealed glass of camphor solution whose crystals were believed to foretell the weather; really a crude thermoscope.

x.d: Storm glass popularised in the 1860s by Admiral Robert FitzRoy, after the Crown gave them to fishing communities following the 1859 storms.
x.dt: camphor, potassium nitrate, ammonium chloride in ethanol and water

kinds.d: Sealed column of liquid with weighted glass bulbs that rise or sink with temperature, each tagged with a reading.

x.d: Floating-bulb thermometer devised by the Accademia del Cimento in Florence and described in 1666; revived as a decorative piece from the 1990s.

v.d: sold by the Natural History Museum, London

x.dt: column height · number of bulbs · coloured liquids

brands.d: London meteorological instrument makers founded by Henry Negretti and Joseph Warren Zambra at Hatton Garden; medal winners at the 1851 Great Exhibition.
London makers of aneroid barometers and barographs, partnered with Taylor Instrument (Tycos) from about 1907; merged 1969.
Patrick Adie's London firm, a principal maker of Kew pattern marine barometers.
Paris instrument firm of Jules and Max Richard, known for recording barometers; RF monogram kept after 1891.
German maker of thermometers, hygrometers and weather stations.

traditions.d: London trade in domestic and marine barometers, with Italian immigrant makers dominant by 1840 and Hatton Garden firms leading the Victorian era.
traditions.tech: mercury tube filling, carved and veneered cases, silvered engraved dials, aneroid movements
traditions.auth: maker's name and address engraved on the dial or register plate; dates from address directories

notes: Barometer: old kind had no source and 4 models; now 6 archetypes (stick, wheel, Admiral FitzRoy, Kew pattern marine, marine, aneroid) with old models as versions (Kew pattern -> P Adie; Stormoguide and Sputnik -> aneroid; 'Banjo barometer' -> wheel barometer alias). Kind s set to the Wikipedia Barometer article (old kind had none). 'Diagonal barometer' alias became the angle type. Barigo, Fischer and Lufft not added: no fetched page (Barigo trade-fair page 404). New kinds Barograph, Storm glass and Galileo thermometer sourced from Wikipedia and Science Museum Group; Galileo thermometer model moved here from Air thermometer (shelf 04_00). Wikipedia names Alexander Cumming (1760s) as first effective recording barograph, so Richard Frères is listed as the 1880s reference maker rather than originator. Tradition: English barometer making.
